summary: Dependency-confusion package exfiltrates host identification data on install
details: @myorder-frontend-commons/analytics ships a poc.js that is wired to the preinstall, install, and postinstall lifecycle hooks in package.json, so running `npm install` auto-executes it. On execution, poc.js collects host identification data (os.hostname(), os.userInfo(), os.platform(), cwd, node version, and CI-related environment markers) and transmits it to attacker-controlled out-of-band collectors: an interactsh subdomain at db4jftohu4noreqdanngpnb3ger45ykrt.oast.fun and a nip.io backup at 80-190-83-27.nip.io. A hex-encoded (hostname|user|version) string is prepended as a DNS subdomain so the same data leaks via DNS resolution even when outbound HTTP egress is blocked. The scope name targets an internal namespace, so build systems that misresolve the internal scope to this public package will execute the exfiltration unattended. The behavior fires at install time without caller consent and sends installer-identifying data to a third-party collector regardless of any "research" framing in the source.
